cost: Exact exponential worst case; conservative O(n^2 2^n) time and O(n^2) auxiliary space including recursion and candidate vectors. n<=64 bounds representation only; no polynomial-time or practical-runtime promise at the cap. Validation O(n+E), E<=n(n-1)/2.
description: Validate a simple undirected graph of at most 64 vertices. Pivoted Bron-Kerbosch maintains clique R, possible P and excluded X; pick the ascending-first pivot maximizing |P intersect N(u)|, branch on P minus N(pivot), recurse with neighbor intersections, then transfer v from P to X. At P=X=empty compare sorted R by cardinality then lexicographic order. Prune only when |R|+|P| is strictly smaller than incumbent.

inverse: Fix sorted output C. Its fiber is every valid graph on the fixed vertex universe in which C is a maximum clique and no lexicographically smaller equal-cardinality clique exists. Missing edges outside C are not recoverable; many distinct graphs share C. Empty C is reachable only for n=0.
limitations: Finite oracle coverage is not proof.
Partial syntax leaves macros opaque; no performance claim.
state: R is a clique and every P/X vertex neighbors all of R; P and X are disjoint. Each maximal clique is considered unless too small to improve cardinality. Equal bounds are retained so lexicographically smaller ties survive. u64 masks represent exactly vertices 0..n; n=64 uses u64::MAX without shifting by 64.
